topics.health: Two structural problems dominate this scope. (1) THE DECISION TREES ARE THE WEAKEST ARTIFACTS, which inverts the intended trust order — standards/decision-trees/README.md:43 instructs agents to cite the tree verbatim BEFORE reading any skill, yet automation-selection.md contains a fabricated limit ('2,000 record cap per interview', :87), a dead branch (Q3 preempts Q6 on callouts), two different coverage gates 70 lines apart (:54 vs :126), and a scheduled-flow threshold 5x apart from its sibling tree flow-pattern-selector.md:56 — which itself self-contradicts inside a single question (Q6 predicate <50k vs branch <250k). The trees should be re-derived FROM the skills, not maintained independently. (2) ORDER-OF-EXECUTION STEP NUMBERS ARE SYSTEMATICALLY STALE across skills/apex/. The corpus is written against an older numbering (before-save flow and before trigger collapsed into 'step 3', after-save at 15, roll-up at 13 or 17, workflow field updates at 9 or 12); the current Apex Developer Guide list is 20 steps with before-save flows at 3, before triggers at 4, workflow rules at 11, Process Builder at 13, after-save flows at 14, parent roll-up at 16. The collapse of steps 3 and 4 into one is what produced the corpus-wide false claim that before-save-flow-vs-before-trigger ordering is indeterminate — a single stale premise that propagated into a whole skill's remediation strategy plus an llm-anti-patterns entry that trains consuming agents to 'detect' and correct the truth. A single-pass renumbering against the live doc would fix five of the thirteen findings above. Two smaller items not worth separate entries: skills/apex/trigger-and-flow-coexistence/references/llm-anti-patterns.md:10 dates before-save flows to 'Spring '22' (they GA'd Spring '20); and automation-selection.md:157 and :160 cite `flow/record-triggered-flows` and `agentforce/agent-creation`, neither of which resolves to a real skill package (the real slugs are flow/record-triggered-flow-patterns and an agentforce equivalent) — a validator gate on decision-tree skill references would catch that class of drift."

Retrieval surfaces one of these, so the user's guest-access advice is a coin flip between "OWD Private, use guest user sharing rules" and "set OWD to Public Read Only." Three concrete follow-ups. (1) skills/security/guest-user-security should be treated as quarantined, not patched — findings 1, 3 and 9 are all in that one file and its core model is wrong; consider merging it into guest-user-security-audit, which is accurate, rather than repairing it. Note the duplicate-audit implication: two skills named guest-user-security and guest-user-security-audit disagree on the fundamentals, which is exactly the near-clone drift the CLAUDE.md duplicate gate exists to prevent. (2) The decision tree itself carries three of the eleven defects (findings 2, 10, 11), and AGENT_RULES instructs agents to read the tree BEFORE the skill — so the tree's restriction-rule "security boundary" claim actively overrides correct skill content in an agent's context window. (3) Two claims I could not settle and flag as unverified rather than wrong: the error string "INVALID_ACCESS_LEVEL, Invalid access level: All" (skills/apex/apex-managed-sharing/references/gotchas.md:37) and the RestrictionRule SOQL field names UserCriteria/RecordCriteria (skills/security/record-access-troubleshooting/references/gotchas.md:208-211, which the author already hedged). topics.health:
Three structural observations for whoever fixes this.

(1) The async-bulk corpus has a single-source-of-truth problem, not a knowledge problem. skills/apex/governor-limits/SKILL.md carries a correct, complete sync/async limits table (SOQL 100/200, heap 6/12, CPU 10k/60k, enqueueJob 50/1, trigger batch 200 but 2,000 for PE/CDC), and skills/apex/apex-queueable-patterns/SKILL.md carries the correct edition-scoped chaining rule with the official quote. Nearly every defect above is a package that re-derived a number locally instead of citing those two. A `dependencies:` edge plus a one-line "canonical limits live in apex/governor-limits" convention would have prevented 8 of the 14. Numbers restated in references/*.md are the worst offenders — SKILL.md files are noticeably more accurate than their own reference files (apex-collections-patterns, apex-email-services and apex-queueable-patterns each disagree with their own references/).

(2) Two numbers in this scope look fabricated rather than mis-remembered, matching the pattern a parallel pass already confirmed. "10 MB heap" appears in skills/apex/apex-email-services/SKILL.md:51 and skills/apex/change-data-capture-apex/SKILL.md:284 — it is not a documented Apex heap value in any context (only 6 and 12 exist). "@future | 10,000 rows arg" in standards/decision-trees/async-selection.md:30 has no documented basis at all. Recommend grepping the whole corpus for `10 MB heap` and for unsourced round numbers in decision-tree matrices before closing this out.

(3) The decision-tree layer is under-verified relative to its authority. AGENT_RULES instructs agents to read the tree BEFORE activating a skill, yet standards/decision-trees/async-selection.md contains two claims (the "5 by default" chain depth and the "10,000 rows arg" ceiling) that its own Related-skills targets contradict, and it carries no Official Sources block of the kind SKILL packages are validated for. Consider extending the `Official Sources Used` validator gate to standards/decision-trees/*.md, and adding a check that every numeric cell in a tree matrix is restated by at least one cited skill.

Not settled, flagged for a follow-up pass rather than asserted here: skills/apex/apex-future-method-patterns/SKILL.md:71 claims @future "failures retry up to 5 times with exponential backoff (platform-managed)" — I could not locate an official statement of a five-retry policy for @future (the documented five-attempt figure is Queueable re-enqueue by a transaction finalizer). Also unverified: standards/decision-trees/async-selection.md:35 "Platform Event | 50k events/hour default" against skills/architect/limits-and-scalability-planning/SKILL.md:163 "250,000 (standard orgs) per 24-hour rolling window" — these are different windows and may both be real allocations, but they sit in the integration hunter's scope, not mine.

topics.topic: LWC-APEX-SECURITY — security enforcement in code (WITH USER_MODE / WITH SECURITY_ENFORCED / stripInaccessible, @AuraEnabled FLS, sharing keyword semantics, Locker vs LWS)
topics.pairs_examined: ~55 claim-pairs across 31 files in skills/apex/, skills/lwc/, skills/security/, skills/architect/, skills/devops/ and standards/decision-trees/sharing-selection.md. Candidate sets built by grepping WITH SECURITY_ENFORCED (77 files), WITH USER_MODE, AccessLevel.USER_MODE, @AuraEnabled+FLS, "inherited sharing", "system mode"/"default", Locker/LWS strictness, and by diffing every API-version/release stamp attached to USER_MODE and SECURITY_ENFORCED. 10 conflicts settled against official docs; 8 apparent conflicts rejected as context-correct.
topics.health:
The dominant failure mode in this scope is not disagreement about security *policy* — every skill agrees you must enforce CRUD/FLS explicitly and default to `with sharing`. It is that the corpus was written across at least four platform eras and nothing carries an API-version qualifier. Three separate platform changes (WITH USER_MODE GA in Spring '23 / API 57, the API 67.0 `with sharing` default for undeclared classes, and the API 67.0 user-mode-by-default for database operations) each landed in one or two skills and were never propagated, so for three of the most-queried questions in the library the corpus now holds two mutually exclusive unconditional answers and retrieval decides which one an agent sees. Recommended systemic fix: require an API-version qualifier on any claim about default execution mode or sharing default, and grep-sweep for the five conflicting USER_MODE version stamps in one pass.

Two findings are fabrications rather than staleness, matching the pattern the parallel passes reported. `System.FlsException` and `System.CrudException` appear five times in skills/security/secure-coding-review-checklist/ and do not exist in the Apex exception hierarchy — the skill instructs developers to catch a type that will not compile. And skills/lwc/visualforce-to-lwc-migration/references/well-architected.md:9 attributes Locker's own mechanism ('secure window proxies') to LWS as the reason LWS is stricter, which is the exact assertion that skills/lwc/lwc-locker-to-lws-migration/references/llm-anti-patterns.md:65 was written to prevent. Two skills in the same domain, one documenting the anti-pattern and the other committing it.

Note for the fix pass: standards/decision-trees/sharing-selection.md is comparatively clean — its sharing-vs-CRUD/FLS orthogonality rule (lines 155-159) is correct and agrees with the skills. Its only defect is the '(Summer '23+)' stamp on WITH USER_MODE at line 145. Because agents are instructed to read the tree before activating a skill, that one-line stamp is worth fixing first even though it is the least severe item on the list.

contradictions.question: Does a before-save record-triggered Flow run before, after, or at the same step as an Apex before trigger — and is the relative order deterministic?
contradictions.statement_a: skills/apex/trigger-and-flow-coexistence/SKILL.md:56 — "Before-save Flows and before Apex triggers both execute at step 3 of the order of execution (after initial record load and before system validation). Salesforce does not guarantee a fixed relative order between a before-save Flow and a before trigger on the same object. If both write to the same field, the result is indeterminate -- whichever runs second silently wins. This is the single most common source of coexistence bugs."
contradictions.statement_b: skills/flow/flow-record-save-order-interaction/SKILL.md:56-57 — "2. Before-save Flows (record-triggered \"Fast Field Updates\")." / "3. Before triggers."
contradictions.official_source_checked: https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_triggers_order_of_execution.htm — step 3 "Executes record-triggered flows that are configured to run before the record is saved."; step 4 "Executes all before triggers." Corroborated by https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.flow_concepts_trigger_guidelines.htm ("you can't prioritize an after-save flow to run before any before-save flows or before an Apex trigger").
contradictions.resolution: The order IS deterministic: before-save flows (step 3) always run before Apex before triggers (step 4). Correct trigger-and-flow-coexistence/SKILL.md:56, its gotchas.md:7 ("Salesforce does not document or guarantee which one runs first... The 'winner' can change between transactions, sandbox refreshes, or platform releases"), examples.md:91, well-architected.md:5 and :20, and llm-anti-patterns.md:15 ("Salesforce does not guarantee their relative order"). The real hazard is the opposite of what the skill states — a before-save Flow can never overwrite a before trigger, but a before trigger will always overwrite a before-save Flow on the same field. Keep the field-ownership-registry remediation; replace the "indeterminate" rationale. Note that trigger-and-flow-coexistence/SKILL.md:171 ("before-save Flows do not re-run" after a workflow field update) IS correct per the same doc — do not remove it while editing.

contradictions.question: Which Flow element rolls back the transaction in a record-triggered flow — Roll Back Records, or Custom Error?
contradictions.statement_a: skills/flow/flow-rollback-patterns/SKILL.md:148 — "In a record-triggered flow processing 200 records, a fault in record #150 rolls back ALL 200 by default. If you need per-record rollback, use Apex (SavePoint) — Flow can't do per-record scope within a batch." (with SKILL.md:65 "Place Rollback Records in the fault path of the element where the critical-failure could occur")
contradictions.statement_b: skills/flow/fault-handling/references/llm-anti-patterns.md:73 — "Use the **Custom Error** element. It is a real Flow Builder element (metadata: `customErrors` on the `Flow` type) that \"shows an error message of your design to the user, and rolls back the current transaction\" — which in a before-save flow means the triggering save is blocked and the user sees your message."
contradictions.official_source_checked: https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.api_meta.meta/api_meta/meta_visual_workflow.htm — FlowRecordRollback / `recordRollbacks`: "An array of nodes for rolling back transactions in the screen flow." Corroborated by https://trailhead.salesforce.com/content/learn/modules/flow-implementation-2/roll-back-changes-after-an-error — "Screen Flows: Use the Roll Back Records element... Record-Triggered Flows: Use the Custom Error element. This element shows an error message of your design to the user, and rolls back the current transaction."
contradictions.resolution: Roll Back Records is a screen-flow element. flow-rollback-patterns must scope itself to screen/autolaunched flows and delete or rewrite the record-triggered claim at SKILL.md:148, and point record-triggered rollback at the Custom Error element (cross-ref flow/fault-handling). The skill cites help.salesforce.com/.../flow_ref_elements_rollback.htm as its Official Source at SKILL.md:197 and well-architected.md:39 while contradicting it, so this is also a contradicts-cited-source defect. Damage is real: an admin who builds an 'atomic' record-triggered flow around an element Flow Builder will not offer ships half-committed parent/child data.

contradictions.question: At what record volume should a scheduled flow escalate to Batch Apex?
contradictions.statement_a: standards/decision-trees/automation-selection.md:84-87 — "Q10. Scheduled job. Does it process > 50k records or run > 5 minutes? | ├── Yes → Batch Apex ... | └── No → Scheduled Flow (simpler, but 2,000 record cap per interview)"
contradictions.statement_b: standards/decision-trees/flow-pattern-selector.md:56 — "├── Yes, < 250k rows and runs under 10min        → Scheduled flow"
contradictions.official_source_checked: https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.flow_considerations_trigger_schedule.htm — "The maximum number of schedule-triggered flow interviews for a single flow is 250,000." "The maximum number of schedule-triggered flow interviews per 24 hours is 250,000, or the number of user licenses in your org multiplied by 200, whichever is greater." "By default, a schedule-triggered flow's query retrieves records in batches of 200, but you can set the batch size from 1 to 200."
contradictions.resolution: Four different thresholds exist in the corpus for the same routing decision: 250k (flow-pattern-selector.md:56, :99, :123), 50k (automation-selection.md:84), 2,000 (skills/flow/scheduled-flows/references/llm-anti-patterns.md:100 and skills/flow/flow-bulkification/references/llm-anti-patterns.md:144), and 500 (skills/flow/scheduled-flows/SKILL.md:111,:114,:239). Worst case: two decision trees that agents are instructed to read BEFORE any skill disagree by 5x. 250,000 is a hard platform ceiling, not a design threshold — using it as the 'stay in Flow' boundary is wrong. Pick one heuristic (the skill-level 500–2,000 band is defensible), state it as a heuristic, and cite the real documented ceilings (250k/flow, 250k or licenses×200 per 24h, batch size 1–200) separately in all four places.

contradictions.question: Does a scheduled flow have a 2,000-record cap per interview?
contradictions.statement_a: standards/decision-trees/automation-selection.md:87 — "└── No   → Scheduled Flow (simpler, but 2,000 record cap per interview)"
contradictions.statement_b: skills/flow/scheduled-flows/SKILL.md (Two Execution Modes table) — "The platform queries matching records and creates **one interview per record**" / "Interviews run in batches (default 200, settable 1–200 in the Start element)"; corroborated at skills/flow/scheduled-flows/references/llm-anti-patterns.md:95 — "An object-selected scheduled flow processes interviews in batches — 200 by default, settable from 1 to 200 in the Start element — and the total interviews per schedule is capped (250,000 per flow; per 24 hours, 250,000 or user licenses × 200, whichever is greater)."
contradictions.official_source_checked: https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.flow_considerations_trigger_schedule.htm — "Each record retrieved by the schedule-triggered flow's query creates one interview." Batch size 1–200, default 200; 250,000 interviews per flow / per 24 hours.
contradictions.resolution: There is no '2,000 record cap per interview'. The claim is incoherent given one interview handles exactly one record; the number appears to be borrowed from the unrelated 2,000-executed-elements-per-interview limit (correctly documented at skills/flow/flow-loop-element-patterns/references/gotchas.md:27). Delete the parenthetical from automation-selection.md:87 and replace with the batch-size-200 / 250k-interview facts.

contradictions.question: Can a before-save (Fast Field Updates) record-triggered flow contain a Get Records element — and therefore carry a fault path?
contradictions.statement_a: skills/flow/fault-handling/references/llm-anti-patterns.md:85 — "fault paths attach to any element that can fail at run time (Get Records, DML, Action, Apex, Subflow), which includes screen flows. The accurate constraint is narrower: a before-save flow has no such elements to attach one to." (reinforced at :87 — "flag any before-save / \"fast field update\" guidance that mentions \"fault connector\" or \"fault path\"")
contradictions.statement_b: skills/flow/flow-governor-limits-deep-dive/SKILL.md:108 — "- Before-Save Validation (3 Get Records = 3 SOQL)"; corroborated by skills/flow/flow-large-data-volume-patterns/SKILL.md:66 — "a record-triggered before-save Flow queries 2,000 Contacts"
contradictions.official_source_checked: https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_concepts_trigger_record.htm (Before-Save Record-Triggered Flows) — before-save flows optimized for fast field updates support Assignment, Decision, Get Records, and Loop; "the flow doesn't contain any Create Records, Action, Delete Records, or Subflow elements."
contradictions.resolution: Get Records IS supported in before-save flows, so a before-save flow does have a failable element and a fault connector can attach to it. Narrow fault-handling's claim to 'a before-save flow contains no DML, Action or Subflow elements' and drop the blanket detection hint at :87, which currently instructs a consuming agent to flag correct guidance (e.g. flow-governor-limits-deep-dive's before-save SOQL budgeting) as an error. Note the same false premise appears in standards/decision-trees/flow-pattern-selector.md:40-41 ("Q3. Do you need any DML, callouts, or cross-object lookups? ├── No → Before-Save"), which wrongly routes any cross-object lookup out of before-save.

contradictions.question: Can a before-save record-triggered flow update a related (non-triggering) record?
contradictions.statement_a: skills/flow/recursion-and-re-entry-prevention/SKILL.md:77 — "...but the chain can still cascade if a before-save Flow updates a related record whose own automation updates back."
contradictions.statement_b: skills/flow/record-triggered-flow-patterns/SKILL.md:228 — "**Before-save cannot replace all trigger behaviors** — if the logic needs related-record work, notifications, or callouts, the design must move to after-save or another boundary."
contradictions.official_source_checked: https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_concepts_trigger_record.htm — "The flow can't update values in records that are related to the triggering record"; the flow "doesn't contain any Create Records, Action, Delete Records, or Subflow elements."
contradictions.resolution: A before-save flow physically cannot perform DML on a related record, so the cascade path described at recursion-and-re-entry-prevention/SKILL.md:77 does not exist. Rewrite that clause to attribute the cascade to the after-save flow or Apex trigger that actually issues the related-record DML. Left as-is, a practitioner debugging a real loop will spend the session inspecting the wrong automation.

contradictions.question: If the requirement needs an HTTP callout, does the automation-selection tree route to Apex or to Flow + invocable Apex?
contradictions.statement_a: standards/decision-trees/automation-selection.md:49-56 — "Q3. Does the logic require any of: ... - HTTP callouts ... ├── Yes  → Apex (trigger + handler + service layer)"
contradictions.statement_b: standards/decision-trees/automation-selection.md:67-69 — "Q6. Does one specific step need code (regex, crypto, complex math, callout) but the orchestration is still simple? ├── Yes  → Flow + InvocableMethod Apex action"; the same file's cheat sheet at :111 lists first choice for "Call an HTTP API" as "Flow → Invocable Apex → `HttpClient`"
contradictions.official_source_checked: https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.flow_concepts_callout.htm (Flow HTTP Callout, native Flow action) plus https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_triggers_order_of_execution.htm (post-commit logic is step 20; callouts are not permitted inline in the save transaction from either Flow or Apex).
contradictions.resolution: Q3 short-circuits before Q6 is ever reached, so the tree's own callout branch at Q6 and its own cheat-sheet row at :111 are unreachable — a routing artifact that agents are told (standards/decision-trees/README.md:43) to cite verbatim as "Per automation-selection.md Q3: this touches HTTP callouts, so Apex is...". contradictions.question: At what record volume does the flow-pattern-selector tree say a scheduled flow is still appropriate?
contradictions.statement_a: standards/decision-trees/flow-pattern-selector.md:54-55 — "Q6. Is the cadence daily / weekly / monthly AND does it process a bounded record set (< 50k) with a predictable query?"
contradictions.statement_b: standards/decision-trees/flow-pattern-selector.md:56 — "├── Yes, < 250k rows and runs under 10min        → Scheduled flow"
contradictions.official_source_checked: https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.flow_considerations_trigger_schedule.htm — 250,000 interviews per flow and per 24 hours (or licenses × 200); batch size 1–200.

Unify Q6's predicate and branch on one number, and align it with automation-selection.md Q10 and skills/flow/scheduled-flows (see the volume-threshold finding above).

contradictions.statement_a: standards/decision-trees/automation-selection.md:54 — "      - unit tests with 90%+ coverage requirements"

contradictions.question: Under Secure Guest User Record Access, how do Experience Cloud guest users get record access — via a Public Read Only OWD, or only via guest user sharing rules?
contradictions.statement_a: skills/security/guest-user-security/SKILL.md:64 — "Guest users can only access records where OWD is Public Read Only or Public Read/Write." (reinforced at :49 "Guest users see records only when OWD is Public Read Only or Public Read/Write", :132 "If the object must be publicly readable, set OWD to Public Read Only. Guest users can then read all records.")
contradictions.statement_b: skills/lwc/experience-cloud-search-customization/references/gotchas.md:17 — "guest users can only see records they explicitly own or that are shared with the Guest User via a sharing rule or sharing set. This overrides the object-level OWD for guest users. An object with OWD set to \"Public Read Only\" is still inaccessible to guests unless a sharing rule or sharing set explicitly grants access."
contradictions.resolution: B is correct on the mechanism. Official: "guest users have org-wide defaults set to Private for all objects"; the setting "is enabled in all Salesforce orgs with Experience Cloud sites and can't be disabled"; guest users "can be granted Read Only access to records only through guest user sharing rules," which are "a special type of criteria-based sharing rule." guest-user-security/SKILL.md is inverted end-to-end and must be rewritten: :49, :63-66, :132-133, :144 and the whole "Configuring OWD for Guest-Accessible Objects" pattern. Aggravating factor — that skill lists "Secure Guest User Record Access" as an Official Source Used (references/well-architected.md:23) while stating the opposite of that page. Two more files inherit the same wrong model and need the same fix: skills/lwc/experience-cloud-api-access/SKILL.md:134 ("Public Read Only external OWD on the object | Only viable path") and skills/lwc/experience-cloud-api-access/references/examples.md:47; also skills/admin/experience-cloud-guest-access/SKILL.md:136 ("external OWD is Public Read Only | Grant Read on guest profile; no sharing rules needed") contradicts the correct guidance in that same file at :84-85.

contradictions.question: Are restriction rules a hard security boundary that excludes records via every entry point, including API and Apex?
contradictions.statement_a: standards/decision-trees/sharing-selection.md:189 — "| Enforcement | Security boundary — user cannot see excluded records via any entry point | UI filter — user can still access excluded records via API or direct URL |"; :192 — "| API impact | Excluded records not returned | No impact |"
contradictions.statement_b: skills/security/record-access-troubleshooting/references/gotchas.md:231 — "A restriction rule is a UI-and-user-mode filter, not a security boundary for code." (and SKILL.md:154 — "They are also bypassed entirely in System Mode, and by `View All Records`/`View All Data`/`Modify All Records`/`Modify All Data`.")
contradictions.resolution: B is correct and verbatim-accurate. Official Considerations: "Restriction rules aren't applied for code executed in System Mode"; users with "View All Records or View All Data permissions can view all records regardless of restriction rules"; "Modify All Records or Modify All Data" holders "can view, edit, and delete all records" regardless. The tree must drop "via any entry point" and add the system-mode / View-All carve-outs, because AGENT_RULES instructs agents to read the tree BEFORE the skill — the tree currently overrides the correct skill guidance with a false assurance. While editing, the tree's Q8 (:96-98, "Do we need to REMOVE access… → Restriction Rule") also needs the supported-object list: restriction rules exist only for "custom objects, external objects, contracts, events, quotes, tasks, time sheets, and time sheet entries" — not Account/Opportunity/Case/Lead — and only "two active restriction rules per object in Enterprise and Developer Editions" / "five" in Performance and Unlimited.

contradictions.question: Does the `with sharing` / `without sharing` keyword change anything for Apex executed by an Experience Cloud guest user?
contradictions.statement_a: skills/security/guest-user-security/SKILL.md:57 — "Every guest user executes Apex in system mode regardless of the `with sharing` or `without sharing` keyword on the class."
contradictions.statement_b: skills/lwc/experience-cloud-api-access/SKILL.md:55 — "Confirm whether the Apex class runs with or without sharing: For guest users, `with sharing` is required. Running `without sharing` on guest-accessible Apex is a critical security violation."
contradictions.resolution: B is correct. Official guest-profile best practices: "If a guest user can execute an `@AuraEnabled` method in an Apex controller used by a Lightning component, always use the 'with sharing' keyword" — which is meaningless advice if the keyword were ignored. Statement A also self-contradicts its own file twice: :99 "Add `with sharing` to the class declaration — this enforces the sharing model so private records are not leaked" and :125 "`without sharing` ignores the sharing model entirely." Delete the :57 claim; the salvageable half is the FLS point (Apex does not enforce FLS regardless of the sharing keyword — true for all users, not guest-specific). skills/security/experience-cloud-security/references/gotchas.md:37 also states correctly that `without sharing` bypasses guest access controls.

contradictions.question: Can Apex managed sharing (inserting __Share rows) grant an Experience Cloud guest user access to a record?
contradictions.statement_a: skills/security/experience-cloud-security/SKILL.md:73 — "Guest users can only access records explicitly shared via Apex sharing, guest sharing rules, or public list views." (repeated at :156 "…guest access requires explicit profile permissions, guest sharing rules, or Apex sharing", and references/gotchas.md:31 "use Apex sharing (`insert new ObjectName__Share(...)`) triggered by a Flow or trigger, or use guest sharing rules if appropriate")
contradictions.statement_b: Salesforce Help, Secure Guest Users' Sharing Settings and Record Access — "Guest users can't be given access to records through manual sharing or Apex managed sharing, and they can't be added to queues or public groups."
contradictions.resolution: The corpus claim is false and dangerous in the opposite direction from most errors here: it sends an engineer down an Apex-sharing path that the platform silently refuses, and worse, it is likely to be 'fixed' at runtime by dropping to `without sharing`. Guest user sharing rules are the only supported grant. Correct :73, :156 and references/gotchas.md:31 in skills/security/experience-cloud-security. Note this skill's Official Sources Used (references/well-architected.md:23-26) does not include the Secure Guest User doc at all — add it.

contradictions.question: Can a Sharing Set grant record access to an Experience Cloud guest user?
contradictions.statement_a: skills/lwc/experience-cloud-search-customization/references/gotchas.md:21 — "create explicit sharing rules (criteria-based or manual) or a Guest User sharing set for each object that guests should be able to search" (same claim at :17)
contradictions.statement_b: skills/security/experience-cloud-security/SKILL.md:156 — "Guest users are excluded from Sharing Sets — Sharing Sets only apply to authenticated portal users (Customer Community, Customer Community Plus, Partner Community). Attempting to grant guest users access via Sharing Sets has no effect"
contradictions.resolution: B is correct. Sharing sets are a high-volume/authenticated-site-user feature keyed off the user's Contact/Account; the Secure Guest User doc enumerates guest user sharing rules as the only grant path and does not include sharing sets. There is no such thing as a "Guest User sharing set." Fix gotchas.md:17 and :21 in experience-cloud-search-customization to say "guest user sharing rule" only. (Note :17 is otherwise the corpus's most accurate statement of the guest model — edit surgically, do not revert the file.)

contradictions.question: Is Salesforce record sharing conjunctive (every layer must allow access) or additive (the most permissive grant wins)?
contradictions.statement_a: skills/apex/salesforce-debug-log-analysis/references/security-sharing.md:7 — "When a user accesses a record, access is granted only if every layer allows it:" — followed by a 10-item list whose items 1-9 are OWD, Role Hierarchy, Sharing Rules, Manual Sharing, Apex Managed Sharing, Teams, Territory Management, Implicit Sharing, Group Membership.
contradictions.statement_b: standards/decision-trees/sharing-selection.md:48 — "Every layer after OWD **broadens** access (except Restriction Rules, which narrow)." (and skills/admin/sharing-and-visibility/SKILL.md:111 — "The most permissive access wins")
contradictions.resolution: B is correct: org-wide defaults set the most restrictive baseline and every subsequent record-level mechanism selectively grants additional access — access is granted if ANY layer grants it. Statement A inverts the model into an AND-gate, under which a Private OWD would defeat every sharing rule. Rewrite security-sharing.md:7 to "access is granted if any layer grants it; only restriction rules subtract." The file's own item 10 ("Restriction Rules (newer): filter visible records further; override sharing that would otherwise grant access") is the only item where the conjunctive framing is right, which is what makes the header sentence look plausible.

contradictions.question: What do the ImplicitParent and ImplicitChild RowCause values mean, and does implicit Account sharing require a master-detail relationship?
contradictions.statement_a: skills/security/record-access-troubleshooting/references/gotchas.md:92 — "The implicit-parent-share behavior (`RowCause = 'ImplicitParent'`) only fires for master-detail." and :95 — "implicit *child-to-parent* shares (`RowCause = 'ImplicitChild'`) only exist between the four hardcoded pairs — Contact→Account, Opportunity→Account, Case→Account, and Order→Account — and they grant Read on the Account when the user has access to the child."
contradictions.statement_b: skills/apex/salesforce-debug-log-analysis/references/security-sharing.md:132 — "If a user has access to an Account, they can see Contacts and Opportunities on that Account per the parent object's sharing setting (View/Edit)." and :136 — "If a user has access to an Opportunity, they get implicit read access to the parent Account."
contradictions.resolution: B is correct; A has the two RowCause labels swapped and adds a false master-detail precondition. Official (Designing Record Access for Enterprise Scale): "Parent implicit sharing is providing access to parent records (account only) when a user has access to children opportunities, cases, or contacts" — i.e. ImplicitParent is the child→parent grant, exactly the behaviour A attributes to ImplicitChild. "Child implicit sharing is providing access to an account's child records" — parent→child, ImplicitChild. Neither requires master-detail: Account↔Contact/Opportunity/Case are standard lookups, and a custom master-detail child has no __Share object at all, so no ImplicitParent row can exist there. Swap the two labels in gotchas.md:92-98 and delete "only fires for master-detail." The gotcha's actual lesson — implicit sharing does not extend to custom child objects — is correct and worth keeping.

contradictions.question: Can AccessLevel = 'All' be set when inserting a __Share row from Apex?
contradictions.statement_a: skills/apex/apex-managed-sharing/SKILL.md:66 — "| `AccessLevel` | String | `Read`, `Edit`, or `All` (All = owner-level; rarely granted via Apex) |"
contradictions.statement_b: skills/apex/apex-managed-sharing/SKILL.md:192 — "Valid values for `AccessLevel` via Apex are `Read` and `Edit`. `All` is reserved for the record owner and cannot be granted via a Share row insert. Attempting to insert a row with `AccessLevel = 'All'` throws a `DmlException`."
contradictions.resolution: B is correct — Apex Developer Guide, Understanding Sharing: Full Access (All) "can only be granted with managed sharing," i.e. by the system, not by a Share insert. The rest of the package already agrees with B (references/gotchas.md:35-37, references/llm-anti-patterns.md:145, templates/apex-managed-sharing-template.md:35 and :166). Fix only SKILL.md:66 — "rarely granted via Apex" is the outlier, and it sits in the field-reference table a code generator reads first. Separately worth verifying before trusting: gotchas.md:37 asserts the specific error string "System.DmlException: INVALID_ACCESS_LEVEL, Invalid access level: All", which I could not confirm in official docs — treat as unverified given this corpus's history of fabricated StatusCodes.

contradictions.question: May the Experience Cloud guest user profile be granted the Create object permission?
contradictions.statement_a: skills/security/guest-user-security/SKILL.md:74 — "Never grant Modify All, View All, Create, Edit, or Delete to the guest profile."
contradictions.statement_b: skills/security/guest-user-security/SKILL.md:145 — "| Guest user needs to create records (e.g., form submission) | Grant Create permission on guest profile for that object only, never Edit/Delete | Minimum privilege; form submissions are Create-only |"
contradictions.resolution: B is correct. Official: "The only object permissions allowed for guest users are read and create"; the prohibitions are "Never assign update or delete permissions to guest users" and "Never assign the View All Records or Modify All Records permission to guest users." Remove "Create" from the :74 never-list. skills/admin/experience-cloud-guest-access/SKILL.md:163 already states the correct nuance ("no Create/Edit/Delete unless a form submission use case requires Create"). Low blast radius — it blocks a legitimate pattern rather than exposing data — but it is the same file as findings 1 and 3, which together make guest-user-security the single least trustworthy package in this scope.

contradictions.question: What is the per-object limit on criteria-based sharing rules?
contradictions.statement_a: standards/decision-trees/sharing-selection.md:113 — "| Limit | Total sharing rules per object (~300 by edition) | None from sharing count; bounded by `__Share` row count |" (the left column is the Criteria-Based Sharing Rule column)
contradictions.statement_b: Salesforce Help, Sharing Rule Considerations / Create Criteria-Based Sharing Rules — the default limit for all sharing rules is 300 per object (raisable to 500 via Support), while criteria-based sharing rules are capped at 50 per object by default (raisable to 200 via Support).
contradictions.official_source_checked: https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.security_sharing_rule_considerations.htm&language=en_US&type=5 (corroborated by the guest-sharing page: guest user sharing rules "count toward the limit of 50 criteria-based sharing rules per object")
contradictions.resolution: The tree overstates the criteria-based ceiling six-fold and misattributes it to edition. Correct to: 300 sharing rules per object total (500 by request), of which at most 50 may be criteria-based (200 by request); the ceiling is a support-raisable default, not an edition tier. This matters because the tree's stated rule at :119 is "Try criteria-based sharing first" — a designer sizing against ~300 will hit the wall at 50. No other file in the corpus states either number, so there is nothing to cross-check against; this is a solo unverified claim in the highest-authority document in scope.

contradictions.question: Are scoping rules a way to GRANT a user access to a record?
contradictions.statement_a: standards/decision-trees/sharing-selection.md:91-94 — "Q7. Does U need access to read only, and only when looking at the record (not in list views or reports)? ├── Yes → Scoping Rules (UI-level filter; NOT a security boundary)" — reached from "START: I need user U to be able to see/edit record R of type T."
contradictions.statement_b: standards/decision-trees/sharing-selection.md:194 — "Choose Restriction Rules for compliance and data segregation. Choose Scoping Rules for usability only." (with :189 "UI filter — user can still access excluded records via API or direct URL")
contradictions.resolution: B is correct; Q7 is a category error inside the access-granting tree. Scoping rules never add access — they narrow the default set a user sees, and they apply specifically to list views and reports ("For list views and reports, you can apply the scope through Metadata API"), which is the exact opposite of Q7's stated condition ("not in list views or reports"). They are also edition-gated: "Available in: Lightning Experience in Performance and Unlimited Editions." Delete Q7 from the grant path and leave scoping rules only in the comparison table at :185-195, with the edition constraint added. An agent following Q7 literally would answer a legitimate access request with a mechanism that grants nothing.

contradictions.question: How many Queueable jobs can System.enqueueJob add in a single SYNCHRONOUS Apex transaction (e.g. a trigger)?
contradictions.statement_a: skills/apex/callout-and-dml-transaction-boundaries/SKILL.md:160 — "**System.enqueueJob counts toward the Queueable limit.** In synchronous transactions, you can enqueue up to 50 Queueable jobs. In a Queueable's own execute, you can enqueue exactly 1 (for chaining)."  (Same claim: skills/apex/apex-future-method-patterns/SKILL.md:63 "the `System.enqueueJob` allocation is 50 synchronously and **1** in an asynchronous context"; skills/apex/governor-limits/SKILL.md:89 "| Queueable jobs enqueued | 50 | 1 child/job |"; skills/integration/retry-and-backoff-patterns/SKILL.md:188 "**`System.enqueueJob()` is limited to 50 per transaction**".)
contradictions.statement_b: skills/apex/async-apex/references/llm-anti-patterns.md:129 — "In a synchronous Apex transaction (trigger, controller), you can only enqueue 1 Queueable job. Enqueuing 2 or more throws `System.LimitException`." (code comment at :123 reads `// Limit: 1 per sync transaction`).  Same error at skills/apex/apex-queueable-patterns/references/llm-anti-patterns.md:179 — "In a trigger context, you can only enqueue 1 queueable job per synchronous transaction (or 1 per `execute` in async). Enqueuing inside a loop with more than 1 qualifying record throws `System.LimitException: Too many queueable jobs added to the queue: 2`."
contradictions.resolution: Official: "Maximum number of Apex jobs added to the queue with System.enqueueJob" = 50 synchronous / 1 asynchronous, and "You can add up to 50 jobs to the queue with System.enqueueJob in a single transaction." B is wrong and is the more prescriptive of the two (it is written as an LLM anti-pattern rule, so it will be quoted back as authority). Rewrite both llm-anti-patterns files to say: the ceiling is 50 in a synchronous transaction and exactly 1 inside an async execute(); the real anti-pattern is per-record enqueue (51 records still blows it, and 50 jobs per trigger is a design smell), not "2 jobs throws". Note also that apex-queueable-patterns is self-inconsistent: SKILL.md:196 correctly scopes single-child chaining to inside execute(), while its own llm-anti-patterns.md:179 extends it to synchronous transactions.

contradictions.question: Does the Salesforce platform enforce a maximum Queueable chain (stack) depth, and if so what is it and in which contexts?
contradictions.statement_a: skills/apex/apex-queueable-patterns/SKILL.md:46 — "How deep can the chain realistically grow? Only Developer Edition and Trial orgs cap it for you — 'the maximum stack depth for chained jobs is 5, which means that you can chain jobs four times.' Production editions enforce no depth limit, so the cap must come from `AsyncOptions.MaximumQueueableStackDepth`." (restated at SKILL.md:64)
contradictions.statement_b: skills/apex/long-running-process-orchestration/SKILL.md:72 — "`AsyncOptions.MaximumQueueableStackDepth` caps the chain length. The platform enforces a maximum of 5 levels in async contexts; in synchronous test contexts the default is 1."  Third and fourth variants: skills/apex/apex-limits-monitoring/references/well-architected.md:12 — "consumes Queueable chain depth (max 5 levels in sync context, unlimited in async)" (exactly inverted from B); skills/apex/billing-integration-apex/references/well-architected.md:7 — "Queueable chains are limited to a depth of 5 concurrent jobs per transaction".
contradictions.resolution: Official Queueable Apex page states both halves: "Because no limit is enforced on the depth of chained jobs, you can chain one job to another" and "For Developer Edition and Trial organizations, the maximum stack depth for chained jobs is 5, which means that you can chain jobs four times." So the 5-deep cap is an EDITION property (DE/Trial), not an async-vs-sync property and not a per-transaction concurrency property. B, and the apex-limits-monitoring and billing-integration-apex variants, are all wrong and all wrong differently. Fix: state the edition rule once (in apex-queueable-patterns) and have the other three cite it; keep `AsyncOptions.MaximumQueueableStackDepth` described as an author-supplied cap, not a platform default. Related soft gap: skills/apex/apex-batch-chaining/SKILL.md:70 says "there is no enforced total chain depth at the platform level" with no DE/Trial carve-out — true in production, false in a scratch/DE org, so it needs the same one-line exception.

contradictions.question: Same question as above, but asked of the decision tree agents are instructed to read BEFORE the skill.
contradictions.statement_a: skills/apex/apex-queueable-patterns/SKILL.md:46 — "Production editions enforce no depth limit, so the cap must come from `AsyncOptions.MaximumQueueableStackDepth`."
contradictions.statement_b: standards/decision-trees/async-selection.md:151 — "**`@future` chain disguised as Queueable.** Enqueueing from Queueable.execute is supported but has depth limits (5 by default). Always check for the terminating condition."
contradictions.resolution: "5 by default" is not a platform default in any edition other than Developer/Trial, and `AsyncOptions.MaximumQueueableStackDepth` has no documented default of 5 (the AsyncOptions reference page publishes no default at all). This is the highest-damage instance because AGENT_RULES routes agents to the tree first: an agent reads "5 by default", concludes runaway chains are self-limiting in production, and stops requiring a terminating condition — which is exactly the failure the skill warns about. Change the tree line to: "no platform depth limit outside Developer Edition / Trial orgs (where it is 5) — you must supply the cap via AsyncOptions.MaximumQueueableStackDepth AND a terminating condition."

contradictions.question: What is the Apex heap ceiling in an ASYNCHRONOUS transaction (Batch execute(), Queueable, @future)?
contradictions.statement_a: skills/apex/governor-limits/SKILL.md:83 — "| Heap size | 6 MB | 12 MB | Large collections and JSON payloads dominate memory |" (sync | async). Same split at skills/apex/governor-limit-recovery-patterns/SKILL.md:52, skills/apex/apex-json-serialization/SKILL.md:159, skills/apex/apex-blob-and-content-version/SKILL.md:45, skills/apex/salesforce-debug-log-analysis/references/governor-and-performance.md:19.
contradictions.statement_b: skills/apex/apex-collections-patterns/SKILL.md:57 — "In a `Database.Stateful` batch job, instance-level Map or List fields persist across every `execute()` call — growing unboundedly until the job finishes or the 6 MB limit kills the transaction. The Apex Developer Guide states the heap limit as 6 MB for synchronous transactions and async transactions alike." (restated as guidance at SKILL.md:47)
contradictions.resolution: Official: "Total heap size" = 6 MB synchronous, 12 MB asynchronous. contradictions.question: When the addressable record set exceeds 50 million, should Batch Apex start() return an Iterable instead of a Database.QueryLocator?

So an Iterable is capped at 50,000 rows, four orders of magnitude BELOW the QueryLocator ceiling. A's routing rule is exactly backwards: following it on a >50M-record set silently processes at most 50,000 records and reports success — a data-completeness failure with no error. Replace A's rule with: past 50M, partition the work (date/Id-range windows, PK chunking, or a driver batch that enqueues per-window QueryLocator batches); an Iterable is for small, non-SOQL or computed collections only. contradictions.question: Bulk API 2.0: does it support serial concurrency mode?

It is not — Bulk API 2.0 only supports parallel mode, and the `concurrencyMode` field is reserved for future use. Serial mode is exclusively a Bulk API v1 feature."

Serial is mandatory. |"

There is no way to request serial mode on a Bulk API 2.0 ingest job. data-loader-batch-window-sizing prescribes 'Bulk V2 serial' as the mitigation for row-lock storms in six places including a row that says "Serial is mandatory" — advice that cannot be executed, so a practitioner following it either silently runs parallel (and gets the UNABLE_TO_LOCK_ROW storm the skill warned about) or wastes a maintenance window. Correct guidance: for genuine serial-mode requirements use Bulk API v1 (or Data Loader's Bulk v1 path with 'Enable serial mode'); with Bulk API 2.0 the levers are pre-sorting the file by parent Id, defer sharing calculations, trigger bypass, and smaller uploads — not a concurrencyMode setting.

contradictions.question: Is the 250,000 asynchronous-Apex-executions-per-24-hours limit per user license or org-wide?

Separately, B's unsourced "Failures retry up to 5 times with exponential backoff" for @future should be sourced or removed — the documented five-retry behaviour belongs to Queueable re-enqueue by a transaction finalizer (correctly stated at skills/apex/apex-queueable-patterns/SKILL.md:82), not to @future.

contradictions.question: What is the heap ceiling for an inbound Email Services handleInboundEmail handler?
contradictions.statement_a: skills/apex/apex-email-services/SKILL.md:51 — "Email Services run synchronously per message. Governor limits apply to the full handler execution: 100 SOQL queries, 150 DML statements, **10 MB heap**. Large attachments (up to 25 MB per email) can breach heap limits quickly."
contradictions.statement_b: skills/apex/apex-email-services/references/gotchas.md:50 — "Loading, decoding, or converting that Blob to a String … inside the synchronous handler can exceed the **12 MB heap limit** …" (and references/examples.md:75 — "risks hitting CPU time limits (10,000 ms for synchronous Apex) and heap limits (**12 MB**)")

Both statements are also internally incoherent with the skill's own framing: it asserts the handler is synchronous (which would make the ceiling 6 MB) while the references quote 12 MB (the async value). Resolve by establishing the handler's actual execution context against the Email Services documentation, then use 6 MB or 12 MB — never 10 MB — and make SKILL.md, gotchas.md and examples.md agree. The 25 MB inbound message size is a separate Email Services limit and is fine as-is.

contradictions.question: What heap ceiling applies to a Change Data Capture / platform event subscriber trigger?
contradictions.statement_a: skills/apex/governor-limits/SKILL.md:83 — "| Heap size | 6 MB | 12 MB |" (sync | async), read together with SKILL.md:92 "**Trigger batch size is 200 for standard DML — but 2,000 for platform events and Change Data Capture events.**"

So 100 SOQL and 150 DML are correct. The heap number is not: the synchronous heap limit is 6 MB, and 10 MB is not a documented Apex heap value (same fabricated figure as the apex-email-services finding above, suggesting one bad source propagated). This is worth fixing carefully rather than reverting — the surrounding claim is a genuine trap the corpus gets right elsewhere only here. Change "10 MB heap" to "6 MB heap (the synchronous value)" and keep the rest, including the 2,000-event batch size which matches skills/apex/governor-limits/SKILL.md:92 and the official "maximum batch size in a platform event trigger is 2,000 event messages."

Because this skill's whole purpose is deciding where to place transaction boundaries in a Queueable/Batch chain, the wrong figure causes steps to be split that did not need splitting — extra chain depth, extra async executions against the 24-hour ceiling. (B's "10-second total callout timeout" is also off: the documented cumulative callout timeout is 120 seconds per transaction, as stated correctly at skills/apex/governor-limits/SKILL.md:85 and skills/apex/apex-callout-retry-and-resilience/SKILL.md:68.)

contradictions.question: Within skills/apex/apex-queueable-patterns, is the single-child enqueue rule a property of async execute() or of any transaction?

This is the same root confusion as finding #1 in this report and should be fixed in one pass across skills/apex/apex-queueable-patterns and skills/apex/async-apex.

contradictions.question: Where should the shared secret used to verify an inbound webhook's HMAC signature be stored?
contradictions.statement_a: skills/integration/webhook-inbound-patterns/references/well-architected.md:18 — "**Storing shared secrets in Apex code** — Hardcoded secrets cannot be rotated without a deployment. Store shared secrets in Custom Metadata or Custom Settings, accessible via SOQL."
contradictions.statement_b: skills/integration/webhook-signature-verification/SKILL.md:50 — "Use Protected Custom Metadata for the secret — not a Custom Setting, which is readable by any user with read."
contradictions.resolution: Salesforce's Secure Coding Guide states that with unprotected custom settings/metadata "everyone in the org can see data values … Use them only when you're storing publicly accessible data," and that outside a managed package you should "use named credentials or encrypted custom fields to store secrets." A's endorsement of Custom Settings and of plain, SOQL-readable Custom Metadata for an HMAC secret is flatly unsafe and must be deleted. B is the safer answer and should be the corpus-wide statement, but B is also incomplete: protected custom metadata only becomes a real boundary when installed as part of a managed package ("only Apex code in the same namespace can see the type") — in an ordinary org any Apex can read it. Corrected corpus line: store inbound webhook secrets in an encrypted custom field or protected CMDT sourced from a managed package; never in a Custom Setting; never in unprotected CMDT; and note that a Named Credential cannot serve here because its secret cannot be read back into Apex to compute the MAC. skills/security/secure-coding-review-checklist/references/llm-anti-patterns.md:145 already states the correct form and should be the canonical wording.

contradictions.question: In a Streaming API / CometD / Pub-Sub subscription, what do replay ID values -1 and -2 mean?
contradictions.statement_a: skills/integration/streaming-api-and-pushtopic/SKILL.md:116-117 — "| `-2` (default) | Receive only new events from this point forward. |" and "| `-1` | Replay all retained events (up to 24 hours). |"

This is the highest-damage finding in the set: a practitioner following streaming-api-and-pushtopic will code -2 believing it means "new only," get a full-backlog replay storm on every restart, or code -1 believing it means "replay everything" and silently lose every event that occurred during an outage. The inversion has propagated through the whole package — fix SKILL.md:25, SKILL.md:108 (the JSON sample uses -1 while the surrounding prose calls it a catch-up subscribe), SKILL.md:117, SKILL.md:149, SKILL.md:187, references/examples.md:7, references/examples.md:50-51, references/gotchas.md:17, and templates/streaming-api-and-pushtopic-template.md:22 and :69. Do NOT touch change-data-capture-integration or platform-events-integration/SKILL.md:90 — those are already right.

contradictions.question: In the platform-events-integration skill package, does replay ID -2 mean "earliest retained event" or "new events only"?

Rewrite lines 27, 54 and 55; leave SKILL.md:90/93/129/179 and references/examples.md:58 alone.

contradictions.question: Can platform event retention be extended past 72 hours by setting a RetainUntilDate field on high-volume platform events?
contradictions.statement_a: skills/integration/platform-events-integration/SKILL.md:100 — "| `RetainUntilDate` support | No (72-hour fixed window) | Yes (configurable retention) |" (Standard vs High-Volume columns); reinforced at SKILL.md:54, :133, :157, :183, :190 and references/examples.md:99 — "entry.RetainUntilDate = DateTime.now().addDays(8); // Retain for 8 days"
contradictions.statement_b: skills/integration/platform-event-schema-evolution/SKILL.md:68 — "High-volume events are stored in the event bus for 72 hours and replayable by Replay ID." and skills/integration/middleware-integration-patterns/SKILL.md:147 — "If the external system is offline for more than 72 hours, events are lost. Middleware's durable queue is not subject to Salesforce's retention window."
contradictions.resolution: `RetainUntilDate` does not exist on Salesforce platform events. The Pub/Sub API guide states "Salesforce stores platform events and change data capture events for 72 hours" and "Salesforce doesn't guarantee the storage of events beyond the retention period of 72 hours" — a fixed window with no configuration surface. The Platform Event Fields page lists only ReplayId and EventUuid as system fields, neither settable by the publisher; there is no RetainUntilDate. Targeted web search returns only AWS S3 Object Lock for that identifier. This is a fabricated field of the same class as the invented StatusCode found by the parallel pass, and it is load-bearing: it appears in the skill's frontmatter trigger keywords (SKILL.md:3), an Apex sample, a REST JSON body, a review-checklist item, and Gotcha 1 — so retrieval on "long event replay window" surfaces a design that cannot be built and whose failure mode is silent event loss at hour 72. Remove the entire RetainUntilDate story from platform-events-integration and from skills/integration/event-driven-architecture-patterns/SKILL.md:71 and :133 ("72 hours (HV: configurable)"). Two adjacent errors in the same table must go with it: SKILL.md:100 gives standard platform events a "72-hour fixed window" when official says "Salesforce stores PushTopic events, generic events, and standard-volume events for 24 hours and high-volume events for 72 hours"; and it assigns 250,000/hour to standard events and "Unlimited" to high-volume, which inverts the allocation table (the 250,000/hour publishing allocation is the high-volume allocation).

contradictions.question: What is the platform event publishing allocation for Enterprise Edition, and over what window?
contradictions.statement_a: skills/integration/event-driven-architecture-patterns/SKILL.md:70 — "Standard event allocation: **250,000 events per 24 hours** on Enterprise and above (lower on lower editions; check the Platform Events Developer Guide for per-edition allocations)."
contradictions.statement_b: skills/integration/platform-events-integration/references/well-architected.md:19 — "Standard events are simpler to set up and sufficient for < 250k events/hour with a 72-hour replay window."
contradictions.resolution: The official Platform Event Allocations table gives 250,000 events published PER HOUR for Enterprise and for Performance/Unlimited (50,000/hour for Developer Edition). B has the right number and the right unit. A is understating org capacity by 24x, and A repeats the error at SKILL.md:134 ("| Standard throughput (events/day) | 250k (Enterprise+) |") and :186 and references/gotchas.md:19 and references/well-architected.md:7 — so a design review run off that skill will wrongly reject an event-driven design as over-allocation. A third value exists in the corpus for the same limit: skills/apex/error-handling-framework/references/gotchas.md:37 says "300,000 events per 24 hours for standard orgs," which matches no official figure at all. Separately, neither skill states the allocation that actually bites in practice — event DELIVERY, which official gives as 25,000/24h for Enterprise, 50,000/24h for Performance/Unlimited, 10,000/24h for Developer, shared between high-volume platform events and CDC. skills/integration/change-data-capture-integration/references/gotchas.md:43-47 is the only place in scope that gets the delivery/publish distinction right and should be the source for the correction.

contradictions.question: Do Bulk API 2.0 requests consume the org's daily API request allocation?
contradictions.statement_a: skills/integration/mulesoft-salesforce-connector/SKILL.md:70 — "| Bulk API 2.0 | High-volume loads (> 10,000 records); asynchronous via jobs. | Does not count against the standard API call limit; has its own daily rolling limit (150M records or 15K batches, whichever is hit first). |" (repeated at SKILL.md:126 and references/well-architected.md:24; also skills/integration/real-time-vs-batch-integration/references/examples.md:108 "It does not count against the REST API daily limit" and skills/security/api-security-and-rate-limiting/SKILL.md:73 "Bulk API does not count against the REST/SOAP daily call limit.")
contradictions.statement_b: skills/data/batch-data-cleanup-patterns/SKILL.md:53 — "Bulk API HARD_DELETE counts against the org's daily API call limits."
contradictions.resolution: Official: "APIs that count toward this allocation include the Lightning Platform REST API, the Lightning Platform SOAP API, Bulk API, Bulk API 2.0, and most Connect REST APIs." B is correct. A is a three-skill-deep false-safety claim that will cause exactly the outage it promises to prevent: a team told Bulk API is outside the daily pool will schedule unbounded intraday bulk syncs and exhaust DailyApiRequests for every other consumer. The accurate framing — which A gets right and should keep — is that Bulk API is far more allocation-EFFICIENT per record (one job request moves up to 10,000 records where REST composite moves 200), and that it additionally has its own separate ceiling. Note the separate-ceiling numbers in A are correct and must not be 'fixed': official states "You can submit up to 15,000 batches per rolling 24-hour period. This allocation is shared between Bulk API and Bulk API 2.0" and "150,000,000 (15,000 batches x 10,000 records per batch maximum)."

contradictions.question: Is there a 10-second timeout ceiling on synchronous Apex callouts?

(repeated at references/gotchas.md:27 — "100 callouts per transaction, 10-second synchronous timeout, 6 MB heap")

A also self-contradicts inside the same file: SKILL.md:73 of the same skill says "Apex orchestration hitting governor limits (100 callouts per transaction, 120-second timeout)." Fix SKILL.md:123 and references/gotchas.md:27 to "120-second per-callout maximum and 120-second cumulative per-transaction ceiling (10-second default until setTimeout is called)." B, plus api-error-handling-design/SKILL.md:133 and skills/integration/api-led-connectivity/references/gotchas.md:7, are already correct.

contradictions.question: Does a /composite/batch request count as one API call, or does each subrequest count separately?

contradictions.statement_b: skills/integration/composite-api-patterns/references/well-architected.md:29 cites "REST API Developer Guide — Composite Batch — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.api_rest.meta/api_rest/resources_composite_batch.htm", which states verbatim: "Each subrequest counts against rate limits."
contradictions.resolution: The two composite resources meter differently and the corpus flattens them. For /composite/ the Composite doc says "The entire series of requests counts as a single call toward your API limits" — so A is correct there and must not be edited. For /composite/batch/ the Batch doc says "Each subrequest counts against rate limits" — so a 25-subrequest batch costs 25 calls, 25x the budget the corpus promises. Scope the claim per resource in composite-api-patterns/SKILL.md:60 and :125, and correct the API-call-cost cell in rest-api-pagination-patterns/references/well-architected.md:49 to "25 calls per composite batch (1 per subrequest)."
