While in composite-api-patterns/SKILL.md, also fix line 130 — "Per-transaction DML row limit (150 statements)" conflates the 150-DML-statement limit with the 10,000-DML-row limit and names neither correctly.

contradictions.question: What is the floor on an org's 24-hour API request allocation?
contradictions.statement_a: skills/integration/soap-api-patterns/SKILL.md:57 — "Enterprise Edition allows up to 1,000 API calls per Salesforce license per 24-hour period (minimum 1,000 total); Developer Edition is limited to 15,000 per day."
contradictions.statement_b: skills/integration/sis-integration-patterns/references/llm-anti-patterns.md:96 — "LLMs do not reliably surface the 24-hour per-org REST API call limit (150,000 calls/day for standard editions) or the 10,000 Apex DML rows-per-transaction limit."
contradictions.resolution: Official gives Enterprise/Professional total allocation as "100,000 + (number of licenses x calls per license type)" with 1,000 calls per Salesforce license, and Developer Edition a flat 15,000. A's per-license rate is right but its "(minimum 1,000 total)" parenthetical understates the floor by two orders of magnitude — an org with one licensed user still gets 100,001, not 1,000 — and a capacity plan built on that floor will reject viable designs. B's "150,000 calls/day for standard editions" is not a limit at all; it is what a 50-license Enterprise org happens to compute to, presented as a fixed platform constant. Replace both with the official formula. Note that soap-api-patterns' Official Sources list (references/well-architected.md:66-73) does not include the API limits page, so this number has no grounding.

contradictions.question: Is the Salesforce org-level API call allocation enforced hourly or over a 24-hour period?
contradictions.statement_a: skills/architect/ai-agent-org-integration-architecture/SKILL.md:188 — "**API call limits are per-org, not per-user** — Salesforce enforces an hourly API call limit at the org level (sum of all API calls from all users, apps, and agents). … Monitor `DailyApiRequests` via the Limits API" (and SKILL.md:149 — "Standard Salesforce REST API has per-org hourly limits based on license count")
contradictions.statement_b: skills/architect/ai-agent-org-integration-architecture/references/gotchas.md:7 — "Salesforce enforces a daily API call limit at the org level (not per-user). The limit is calculated based on the number of full-use licenses in the org (typically 1,000 calls per license per 24-hour period for Enterprise Edition)."
contradictions.resolution: The allocation is a 24-hour allocation; the cheat sheet's whole table is "calls per license per 24-hour period." B is correct. A is wrong twice in one skill and self-refuting inside a single sentence — it claims an hourly limit and then tells the reader to monitor `DailyApiRequests`. A high-volume agent sized against a phantom hourly bucket will be provisioned roughly 24x too generously and exhaust the real daily allocation. Fix SKILL.md:149 and :188 to "24-hour"; leave gotchas.md alone. (There IS a genuine hourly constraint in this neighbourhood — the 250,000/hour platform event publishing allocation — but it has nothing to do with REST API calls, and conflating them is how this error most likely arose.)

contradictions.question: Is Custom Metadata ever an acceptable home for an integration secret?
contradictions.statement_a: standards/decision-trees/integration-pattern-selection.md:150-151 — "2. Never store an API key in Custom Setting, Custom Metadata, or Apex source. Use External Credentials → Principals."
contradictions.statement_b: skills/integration/webhook-signature-verification/SKILL.md:40 — "Store the shared secret in Protected Custom Metadata (`Webhook_Secret__mdt.Value__c`) or a Named Credential with a dummy endpoint." (and SKILL.md:32, :50)
contradictions.resolution: This is the worst structural shape in the set, because AGENT_RULES instructs agents to read the tree BEFORE the skill, so the tree's absolute wins by construction. The tree's rule is correct and should stay for its actual scope — OUTBOUND callout credentials, where External Credential principals are the right answer precisely because the secret is injected by the platform and never readable. It is unachievable for the INBOUND case B addresses: verifying an HMAC requires reading the secret into Apex to recompute the MAC, and an External Credential secret cannot be read back, which is why B resorts to "a Named Credential with a dummy endpoint." Resolution: scope the tree rule explicitly ("Never store an OUTBOUND callout credential in a Custom Setting, Custom Metadata, or Apex source") and add an inbound branch citing the official guidance the corpus never mentions anywhere — "Outside of a managed package, use named credentials or encrypted custom fields to store secrets" — with protected CMDT acceptable only when packaged, since official qualifies it as "installed as part of a managed package … only Apex code in the same namespace can see the type." Do not delete B; do not weaken the tree's outbound rule.

contradictions.question: What exception does a SOQL query with WITH USER_MODE throw when the running user lacks access to a queried field?
contradictions.statement_a: skills/security/secure-coding-review-checklist/references/gotchas.md:7 — "When a SOQL query with `WITH USER_MODE` encounters a field the running user cannot access, the platform throws a `System.FlsException` at runtime" (repeated at SKILL.md:87, SKILL.md:159 "throws `System.FlsException` or `System.CrudException`", gotchas.md:11 "Wrap queries in try-catch blocks that handle `System.FlsException` and `System.CrudException`", references/well-architected.md:9)
contradictions.statement_b: skills/apex/apex-stripinaccessible-and-fls-enforcement/references/well-architected.md:14 — "| `WITH USER_MODE` (THROW-on-inaccessible) | Loud — caller gets `QueryException` and knows immediately |"
contradictions.resolution: `System.FlsException` and `System.CrudException` do not exist. The Apex Reference built-in exception list contains DmlException, QueryException, NoAccessException etc. — neither FlsException nor CrudException appears anywhere in it. QueryException is the correct type, and it carries the dedicated `getInaccessibleFields()` method precisely for field-level-security failures. Replace all five occurrences in skills/security/secure-coding-review-checklist/ with `System.QueryException` (and `System.DmlException` for user-mode DML), and note `getInaccessibleFields()`. This is not cosmetic: a developer following gotchas.md:11 writes `catch (System.FlsException e)`, which fails to compile — the most likely reaction is to delete the enforcement rather than the catch block.

contradictions.question: In what mode do Apex database operations (including those behind an @AuraEnabled method) run by default?
contradictions.statement_a: skills/apex/soql-security/references/gotchas.md:38-40 — "## 4. `@AuraEnabled` Methods Run in System Context By Default / Even when a user calls an `@AuraEnabled` method, Apex runs in system context unless: - The class is declared `with sharing` … - The query uses `WITH USER_MODE` or `WITH SECURITY_ENFORCED`" (same claim, unqualified, at skills/apex/soql-fundamentals/references/well-architected.md:5 "Every SOQL query in Apex runs in system mode by default, bypassing FLS and object-level security")
contradictions.statement_b: skills/apex/apex-security-patterns/SKILL.md:141 — "7. **A trigger's `without sharing` context does not disable FLS** — trigger DML still runs in user mode unless system mode is explicitly requested." (and SKILL.md:63 "database operations run in user mode unless system mode is explicitly specified")
contradictions.resolution: The answer is API-version-dependent and neither skill states the version. Official: "In API version 67.0 and later, Apex runs in user mode by default, meaning that the current user's permissions and field-level security (FLS) are enforced during code execution"; "Database operations only ignore FLS and object permissions if you explicitly set them to run in system mode." API 66.0 and earlier: system mode is the default. So statement A is correct only for API <= 66.0 and statement B only for API >= 67.0, and both are asserted unconditionally. Add the API-version qualifier to both, and to skills/apex/salesforce-debug-log-analysis/references/security-sharing.md:33 ("Apex triggers run in system mode by default") and skills/architect/security-architecture-review/SKILL.md:89 ("Apex running in system context bypasses FLS by default"). Damage runs both ways: an agent trusting B on a legacy API-55 class omits enforcement entirely.

contradictions.question: How do you enforce user-mode FLS/CRUD on a dynamic SOQL query?
contradictions.statement_a: skills/apex/dynamic-apex/SKILL.md:229 — "3. **`WITH USER_MODE` in dynamic SOQL does not exist — use `WITH SECURITY_ENFORCED` or explicit FLS checks** — `WITH USER_MODE` is only valid in static SOQL as of Spring '25. Dynamic SOQL queries must enforce FLS via explicit `DescribeFieldResult` checks or `Security.stripInaccessible()` on results."
contradictions.statement_b: skills/apex/soql-security/references/llm-anti-patterns.md:81-91 — "For dynamic SOQL with user-mode enforcement, you must use `Database.query(query, AccessLevel.USER_MODE)`. … `List<Account> results = Database.query(query, AccessLevel.USER_MODE);`"
contradictions.resolution: The Dynamic SOQL page documents exactly the mechanism statement A omits: "In API version 55.0 and later, you can use the accessLevel parameter to run the query operation in user or system mode" — `List<sObject> sobjList = Database.query(string, AccessLevel.USER_MODE);`. Statement A's enumerated remedies ("must enforce FLS via explicit DescribeFieldResult checks or Security.stripInaccessible") exclude the documented, one-argument, canonical control and steer generated code toward hand-rolled describe loops that miss fields. The "as of Spring '25" stamp is also unsupported — user-mode Database operations went beta Summer '22 (API 55) and GA Spring '23. Rewrite dynamic-apex/SKILL.md:229 to point at the accessLevel parameter; keep the (correct) separate point that the clause is not an injection defence.

contradictions.question: Can an Apex trigger declare a sharing keyword, and what happens if it doesn't?
contradictions.statement_a: skills/security/secure-coding-review-checklist/references/gotchas.md:15-21 — "## Gotcha 2: Apex Triggers Default to without sharing When No Keyword Is Declared … **When it occurs:** Every trigger execution where the developer did not explicitly declare `with sharing` or `without sharing`." (and SKILL.md:158 "Apex triggers that omit the sharing keyword run in system context with full data visibility")
contradictions.statement_b: skills/apex/apex-security-patterns/SKILL.md:63 — "Apex triggers cannot carry an explicit sharing keyword and always run implicitly in a `without sharing` context. That does not mean trigger DML ignores field and object permissions: database operations run in user mode unless system mode is explicitly specified, and user mode overrides the trigger's `without sharing` context for the operation."
contradictions.resolution: Official: "Apex triggers can't have an explicit sharing declaration. Triggers always run implicitly in a without sharing context" and "database operations within trigger bodies … run in user mode unless system mode is explicitly specified. User mode overrides the trigger's without sharing context." Statement A presents the sharing mode as a developer choice that was omitted — there is no choice — and its remedy ("Every trigger execution where the developer did not explicitly declare `with sharing`") describes an action that produces a compile error. Rewrite gotcha 2 to say triggers cannot declare sharing at all and that the correct control is the handler class plus explicit access mode on the DML/SOQL.

contradictions.question: Is Lightning Web Security stricter or less restrictive than Lightning Locker?
contradictions.statement_a: skills/lwc/visualforce-to-lwc-migration/references/well-architected.md:9 — "Lightning Web Security (LWS) provides stricter sandboxing than Locker Service: Trusted Types enforcement, secure window proxies, and stricter cross-origin controls."
contradictions.statement_b: skills/lwc/lwc-locker-to-lws-migration/SKILL.md:63 — "**The most common wrong assumption.** That LWS is \"stricter\" than Locker. It is not — LWS is **less intrusive at runtime** (no SecureElement proxy wrapping every DOM node) but **more strict at the realm boundary**" (and references/llm-anti-patterns.md:65 names asserting-LWS-is-stricter as Anti-Pattern 4)
contradictions.resolution: Official comparison: "Lightning Web Security doesn't use secure wrappers, which can reduce performance, unlike Lightning Locker" — Locker is the model that replaces window/document/element with secure wrappers; LWS gives each namespace a detached JS sandbox and "has fewer restrictions and more functionality than Lightning Locker." Statement A is wrong twice over: it inverts the direction, and it attributes Locker's own mechanism ("secure window proxies") to LWS as LWS's differentiator. Fix visualforce-to-lwc-migration/references/well-architected.md:9 to match lwc-locker-to-lws-migration's framing. Note the perverse effect: skills/lwc/lwc-locker-to-lws-migration/references/llm-anti-patterns.md:65 exists specifically to stop an agent producing statement A — and another skill in the same domain produces it.

contradictions.question: What does an Apex class with no sharing keyword run as?
contradictions.statement_a: skills/apex/apex-security-patterns/SKILL.md:51 — "In API version 67.0 and later, a class with no explicit sharing declaration runs in `with sharing` mode." (repeated SKILL.md:123, SKILL.md:139, references/gotchas.md:35-39)
contradictions.statement_b: skills/apex/apex-with-without-sharing-decision/SKILL.md:106-112 — "A class with no sharing keyword is **not equivalent to `with sharing`**. Historically it ran effectively as `without sharing`. Since API v34, when called from a Lightning context (`@AuraEnabled`, `@RemoteAction`) it runs as `with sharing`, but in many other contexts (called from a `without sharing` class, anonymous Apex, some legacy entry points) it still runs as `without sharing`."
contradictions.resolution: Official: "In API version 67.0 and later, classes without an explicit sharing declaration run in with sharing mode." Statement B is correct only for API 66.0 and earlier and carries no version qualifier, so it will be read as current. Both skills reach the same practical advice ("never ship a bare class"), so the damage is limited to a stale mechanism claim — but B is also the skill an agent lands on when the query is literally "with sharing vs without sharing", so it is the one more likely to be cited. Add the API 67.0 boundary to apex-with-without-sharing-decision/SKILL.md:106.

contradictions.question: What is the default sharing mode for an undeclared Apex class in "newer contexts"?
contradictions.statement_a: skills/security/secure-coding-review-checklist/SKILL.md:44 — "Identify the Apex sharing model: classes declared `with sharing`, `without sharing`, `inherited sharing`, or no keyword (defaults to `without sharing` in triggers, `inherited sharing` in newer contexts)."
contradictions.statement_b: skills/apex/apex-security-patterns/SKILL.md:51 — "In API version 67.0 and later, a class with no explicit sharing declaration runs in `with sharing` mode."
contradictions.resolution: There is no version of the platform in which an undeclared class defaults to `inherited sharing`. Official states the API 67.0+ default is `with sharing`, and pre-67 the class runs in the caller's established mode (defaulting to without sharing at an entry point). `inherited sharing` is only ever an explicit declaration. This matters because a reviewer following statement A will read an undeclared class as "safely inheriting" and pass it, when on an API-66 org it is effectively `without sharing`. Also note statement A's "defaults to without sharing in triggers" is the same impossible-keyword framing flagged above — triggers cannot declare sharing.

contradictions.question: Which Salesforce release / API version introduced WITH USER_MODE?
contradictions.statement_a: skills/apex/soql-security/references/gotchas.md:32 — "| Available since | Always | Winter '23 (API 56) |" (and gotchas.md:21 "`WITH USER_MODE` (Winter '23+)")
contradictions.statement_b: skills/apex/apex-stripinaccessible-and-fls-enforcement/SKILL.md:173 — "| Running on API < 48 | `WITH SECURITY_ENFORCED` | stripInaccessible introduced in API 45, USER_MODE in 58 |" (and skills/apex/apex-dynamic-soql-binding-safety/SKILL.md:122 "`WITH USER_MODE` (API 58+)")
contradictions.resolution: Five different stamps exist in the corpus for one feature: "Winter '23 (API 56)" (soql-security/references/gotchas.md:32), "API 58 / Summer '23" (apex-stripinaccessible SKILL.md:173, apex-dynamic-soql-binding-safety SKILL.md:122), "Summer '23+" (standards/decision-trees/sharing-selection.md:145), "API 56.0+, Summer '22" — internally impossible, since API 56.0 is Winter '23 (skills/architect/security-architecture-review/SKILL.md:89), and "Spring '20+" (skills/security/secure-coding-review-checklist/SKILL.md:53). Official timeline: the accessLevel parameter arrived in API 55.0 (Summer '22, beta — "In API version 55.0 and later, you can use the accessLevel parameter"), beta extended in Winter '23, and user-mode database operations went GA in Spring '23 (release 242, API 57.0). Standardise on "beta Summer '22 (API 55), GA Spring '23 (API 57)". Worst offender is the decision tree: agents are instructed to read standards/decision-trees/sharing-selection.md BEFORE the skill, and it carries the wrong stamp.

contradictions.question: Is WITH SECURITY_ENFORCED still available and usable?
contradictions.statement_a: skills/apex/apex-stripinaccessible-and-fls-enforcement/references/well-architected.md:16 — "| `WITH SECURITY_ENFORCED` (legacy) | Available pre-API 58 | Deprecated in spirit; USER_MODE supersedes it |" (and SKILL.md:102 "| Backwards compat to API 47 or earlier | `WITH SECURITY_ENFORCED` (legacy) |")
contradictions.statement_b: skills/apex/soql-security/SKILL.md:73 — "| CRUD/FLS bypass | Apex exposes fields or objects the running user should not access | `WITH USER_MODE`, `WITH SECURITY_ENFORCED`, or `stripInaccessible()` |" — offered as a current, co-equal option (same posture in skills/lwc/lwc-security/SKILL.md:264 and :278, which require it in the review checklist)
contradictions.resolution: WITH SECURITY_ENFORCED is documented as current in the SOQL/SOSL Reference and is not marked deprecated in any API version; "Available pre-API 58" reads as "unavailable from API 58", which is false. What the docs actually say is a recommendation, not a removal: "Salesforce recommends that you enforce field- and object-level security permissions by using WITH USER_MODE instead of WITH SECURITY_ENFORCED because it has fewer limitations." Replace "Available pre-API 58" with "Still supported; Salesforce recommends WITH USER_MODE instead — fewer limitations", and drop the "API 47 or earlier" backwards-compat framing.

contradictions.question: Can WITH USER_MODE appear inside a dynamic SOQL string passed to Database.query / queryWithBinds?
contradictions.statement_a: skills/apex/apex-dynamic-soql-binding-safety/SKILL.md:122 — "Both clauses are valid INSIDE a dynamic query string." (and SKILL.md:175 builds a string ending `' WITH USER_MODE LIMIT 200'` and passes it to queryWithBinds)
contradictions.statement_b: skills/apex/soql-security/references/llm-anti-patterns.md:78-81 — "// WITH USER_MODE cannot be appended to Database.query string … it is a compile-time clause for inline SOQL, not for dynamic `Database.query()`"
contradictions.resolution: I could not find an official statement either permitting or forbidding a WITH USER_MODE clause inside a dynamic query string — the Dynamic SOQL page documents only the accessLevel parameter, and the SOQL WITH reference documents the clause without addressing dynamic construction. Both skills state their position as fact with no citation, and apex-dynamic-soql-binding-safety/SKILL.md:175 ships runnable example code that depends on its position being right. Resolution should be to drop the unsourced absolute in both places and state only the documented mechanism: `Database.query(q, AccessLevel.USER_MODE)` / `Database.queryWithBinds(q, binds, AccessLevel.USER_MODE)` (API 55.0+). Note that apex-dynamic-soql-binding-safety/SKILL.md:124 already recommends exactly that ("Prefer `Database.queryWithBinds(..., AccessLevel.USER_MODE)` over an in-string `WITH USER_MODE`"), so removing the disputed sentence costs the skill nothing. Flag for a follow-up pass with org access to compile-test.

high_severity.question: Which Flow element rolls back the transaction in a record-triggered flow — Roll Back Records, or Custom Error?

If you need per-record rollback, use Apex (SavePoint) — Flow can't do per-record scope within a batch." (with SKILL.md:65 "Place Rollback Records in the fault path of the element where the critical-failure could occur")

It is a real Flow Builder element (metadata: `customErrors` on the `Flow` type) that \"shows an error message of your design to the user, and rolls back the current transaction\" — which in a before-save flow means the triggering save is blocked and the user sees your message."

The skill cites help.salesforce.com/.../flow_ref_elements_rollback.htm as its Official Source at SKILL.md:197 and well-architected.md:39 while contradicting it, so this is also a contradicts-cited-source defect. high_severity.question: Under Secure Guest User Record Access, how do Experience Cloud guest users get record access — via a Public Read Only OWD, or only via guest user sharing rules?
high_severity.statement_a: skills/security/guest-user-security/SKILL.md:64 — "Guest users can only access records where OWD is Public Read Only or Public Read/Write." (reinforced at :49 "Guest users see records only when OWD is Public Read Only or Public Read/Write", :132 "If the object must be publicly readable, set OWD to Public Read Only. Guest users can then read all records.")
high_severity.statement_b: skills/lwc/experience-cloud-search-customization/references/gotchas.md:17 — "guest users can only see records they explicitly own or that are shared with the Guest User via a sharing rule or sharing set. This overrides the object-level OWD for guest users. An object with OWD set to \"Public Read Only\" is still inaccessible to guests unless a sharing rule or sharing set explicitly grants access."
high_severity.resolution: B is correct on the mechanism. Official: "guest users have org-wide defaults set to Private for all objects"; the setting "is enabled in all Salesforce orgs with Experience Cloud sites and can't be disabled"; guest users "can be granted Read Only access to records only through guest user sharing rules," which are "a special type of criteria-based sharing rule." guest-user-security/SKILL.md is inverted end-to-end and must be rewritten: :49, :63-66, :132-133, :144 and the whole "Configuring OWD for Guest-Accessible Objects" pattern. Aggravating factor — that skill lists "Secure Guest User Record Access" as an Official Source Used (references/well-architected.md:23) while stating the opposite of that page. Two more files inherit the same wrong model and need the same fix: skills/lwc/experience-cloud-api-access/SKILL.md:134 ("Public Read Only external OWD on the object | Only viable path") and skills/lwc/experience-cloud-api-access/references/examples.md:47; also skills/admin/experience-cloud-guest-access/SKILL.md:136 ("external OWD is Public Read Only | Grant Read on guest profile; no sharing rules needed") contradicts the correct guidance in that same file at :84-85.

high_severity.question: Are restriction rules a hard security boundary that excludes records via every entry point, including API and Apex?
high_severity.statement_a: standards/decision-trees/sharing-selection.md:189 — "| Enforcement | Security boundary — user cannot see excluded records via any entry point | UI filter — user can still access excluded records via API or direct URL |"; :192 — "| API impact | Excluded records not returned | No impact |"

(and SKILL.md:154 — "They are also bypassed entirely in System Mode, and by `View All Records`/`View All Data`/`Modify All Records`/`Modify All Data`.")

The tree must drop "via any entry point" and add the system-mode / View-All carve-outs, because AGENT_RULES instructs agents to read the tree BEFORE the skill — the tree currently overrides the correct skill guidance with a false assurance. high_severity.question: Does the `with sharing` / `without sharing` keyword change anything for Apex executed by an Experience Cloud guest user?
high_severity.statement_a: skills/security/guest-user-security/SKILL.md:57 — "Every guest user executes Apex in system mode regardless of the `with sharing` or `without sharing` keyword on the class."
high_severity.statement_b: skills/lwc/experience-cloud-api-access/SKILL.md:55 — "Confirm whether the Apex class runs with or without sharing: For guest users, `with sharing` is required. Running `without sharing` on guest-accessible Apex is a critical security violation."
high_severity.resolution: B is correct. Official guest-profile best practices: "If a guest user can execute an `@AuraEnabled` method in an Apex controller used by a Lightning component, always use the 'with sharing' keyword" — which is meaningless advice if the keyword were ignored. Statement A also self-contradicts its own file twice: :99 "Add `with sharing` to the class declaration — this enforces the sharing model so private records are not leaked" and :125 "`without sharing` ignores the sharing model entirely." Bulk API 2.0 upload size stated as 150 MB (real-time-vs-batch-integration/references/examples.md:73, sis-integration-patterns/references/llm-anti-patterns.md:102) vs 100 MB raw / 150 MB base64 (bulk-api-and-large-data-loads/SKILL.md:47, :113, :168). Not a contradiction — official gives the ceiling as "150 MB per job" measured on base64-encoded content and then advises "upload data that does not exceed 100 MB" because encoding adds ~50%. The 150 MB figure is the documented limit; the 100 MB figure is the documented practical guidance. Both belong in the corpus.

Replay ID -1 recommended as the reconnect target in change-data-capture-integration/references/gotchas.md:57 ("re-subscribe at tip (-1)") and flagged as an anti-pattern in the same package's llm-anti-patterns.md:51 ("Stateless Replay — Reconnecting with -1 Every Time"). Context-correct, not conflicting: -1 is the right choice AFTER a deliberate Bulk API re-sync has closed the gap, and wrong as a default startup behaviour that skips the gap. The CDC package handles this distinction well and should not be flattened. Same reasoning protects the checker scripts in both event skills that warn on hardcoded -1 "without an explanatory comment" rather than banning it.

Retry classification: retry-and-backoff-patterns/references/well-architected.md:24 ("Only retry on 429, 503, 5xx (excluding 501), and System.CalloutException") vs outbound-webhook-from-salesforce/references/llm-anti-patterns.md:27 ("retry 5xx, 408, 429 only. 4xx is permanent") vs api-error-handling-design/SKILL.md:222 (retry-safe = 429, 500, 503, timeout; permanent = 400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 422). Three different granularities of the same policy, mutually consistent — 408 Request Timeout is a legitimate documented exception to "4xx is permanent" and its presence in one list and absence from another is a completeness gap, not a contradiction.

Secret storage for OUTBOUND webhook HMAC signing: outbound-webhook-from-salesforce/references/llm-anti-patterns.md:29-35 ("Anti-Pattern 4: Secret In Custom Metadata → Correct pattern: External Credential inside the Named Credential") vs webhook-signature-verification's Protected CMDT recommendation. Different direction, different mechanism — rejected as a contradiction. Flagging separately for a future pass rather than as a cross-skill conflict: the outbound advice is likely unworkable on its own terms, because signing an outbound body with HMAC also requires reading the secret into Apex, which an External Credential does not permit; it only injects credentials into headers. That is a single-skill correctness question, not a disagreement between skills.

WITH USER_MODE (throw) vs Security.stripInaccessible (strip-and-continue) — apex-stripinaccessible-and-fls-enforcement/SKILL.md:95-105 recommends USER_MODE for reads and stripInaccessible for user-supplied DML, while secure-coding-review-checklist/references/gotchas.md:11 recommends stripInaccessible 'when graceful degradation is required'. These are the same rule stated from two directions (fail-fast vs degrade), both documented, and complementary. Do NOT collapse them into one recommendation.

'@AuraEnabled does not bypass CRUD/FLS' (lwc/lwc-quick-actions/SKILL.md:84) vs '@AuraEnabled methods are callable by any user including guest users' (lwc/lwc-security/SKILL.md:287). These answer different questions — permission model vs reachability — and are both true. Not a conflict.

'WITH USER_MODE enforces both sharing rules and FLS/CRUD' (apex-with-without-sharing-decision/SKILL.md:116-120) vs 'FLS and CRUD are a separate enforcement concern... not controlled by these keywords' (same file, line 76). 'USING SCOPE is a filter, not a security boundary' (apex/soql-using-scope-clause/SKILL.md:46, :85, :174) alongside skills that treat WITH USER_MODE as the security control. Orthogonal mechanisms, explicitly documented as such by the skill itself. Correct as written.

'Inner classes run in system mode regardless of outer-class sharing' (apex/apex-wrapper-class-patterns/SKILL.md:176) vs outer-class 'with sharing' guidance elsewhere. Official sharing-keywords doc: 'Inner classes don't adopt the sharing mode of the container class.' The wrapper skill matches the platform. Do not 'fix' it to say inner classes inherit.

'stripInaccessible does not restore sharing' (apex/soql-security/SKILL.md:118) vs 'stripInaccessible enforces CRUD/FLS' (apex-stripinaccessible-and-fls-enforcement/SKILL.md:3).
